title: A carried gate counts writes made after its launcher finished, until the host next polls it, as writes "before it settled"
outcome:
Reported by Engram::Opus (session-7284) through TermAl mailbox 37bcca97, message #159, 2026-10-01, host 8e8358a.

A background full gate was launched at 2026-10-01T01:30:27.848Z in Engram's named-root-assessment worktree. Its launcher finished at 01:41Z: all 9 stages passed, and its own freeze check matched at completion.

At about 01:45Z the session edited a file for its next item. The host then refused the gate: "a file in its worktree changed: …\src\mcp.rs.tmp.70588.7f5cb3752adc", which is the edit's temporary file.

So the host treats the run as unsettled after the launcher has written its terminal result. It looks as if the host settles a carried run only when it next polls carried runs, at a turn checkpoint, and fences every write up to then.

Expected: the run settles at the launcher's terminal result, its results.json completion time. A write after that time does not refuse it, even if the host learns of the completion later. If the delay is intended, the refusal line and docs/test.md must say what "settled" waits for, so that a session knows not to edit until then.

Related: w-072e84b182c7 (silence when not recorded) and the keep-focus memory, which already tells holders to wait for the record before touching anything.
acceptance: A carried gate whose launcher wrote its terminal result before a later write in its worktree is not refused for that write, even when the host processes the completion after the write; a test covers it.
A write between launch and the launcher's terminal result still refuses the credit; a test covers it.
